calls.summary: Maria Delgado called about her daughter's spinal curve and wanted a scoliosis evaluation at the St. Louis location. Agent Rosey reviewed the referral, confirmed insurance was not required, and booked an appointment for a bracing assessment. Maria left reassured and thanked the team warmly.

James Whitaker phoned to learn about cleft lip and palate repair for his infant son. Agent Lila explained the multi-stage surgical plan and feeding support, then scheduled an appointment with the craniofacial team. James was grateful for the clear guidance.

Patricia Nolan called to donate to the Love to the Rescue campaign in honor of a family friend. Agent Oscar processed her one-time gift and shared how to set up recurring giving. Patricia said she would consider the Fez Fund Drive next year.

Andre Coleman called as a new family seeking pediatric orthopedic care for his son after a sports injury. Agent Mary collected his contact details, the child's history, and referral information, then scheduled a new patient consultation. Andre confirmed the appointment date and the intake paperwork to complete beforehand.

Denise Fowler called about a custom prosthetic device for her daughter who is outgrowing her current limb. Agent Lee explained the POPS fitting and fabrication process and booked an appointment for a growth adjustment fitting. Denise was pleased with how quickly it was arranged.

Robert Aguilar phoned to arrange a follow-up for his son's burn scar revision and laser reconstruction. Agent Sue reviewed the treatment notes and scheduled an appointment with the plastic surgery team. Robert appreciated the reminder about wound care instructions.

Karen Bishop called with a billing question about a statement she received after her son's therapy sessions. Agent Mike explained the charges and noted that financial assistance may apply. Karen wanted the itemized breakdown emailed before deciding anything.

Thomas Reyes called to check the status of a custom scoliosis brace that was being fabricated. Agent Jennifer looked up the order and confirmed it was still in production with an estimated ready date. Thomas was frustrated by the wait but understood the timeline.

Angela Simmons phoned to reschedule an existing appointment for her daughter's rehabilitation therapy because of a work conflict. Agent Rose found a later slot but Angela needed to confirm with her spouse first. No new visit was booked on the call.

Victor Hollis called because his son's prosthetic device needed a repair after the socket cracked. Agent Oscar logged the issue and arranged for the POPS team to inspect it, but the earliest slot was two weeks out. Victor was unhappy about the delay.

Sharon Pruitt called upset that her monthly gift to donate had been charged twice. Agent Lila apologized, confirmed the duplicate, and started a refund for the second charge. Sharon wanted written confirmation before ending the call.

Gregory Mason complained about a long wait during a recent clinic visit for his son's gait lab study. Agent Lee documented the feedback and offered to escalate it to the location manager. Gregory remained dissatisfied and did not book anything further.

Nicole Barrera called to cancel an upcoming burn care follow-up because the family was relocating out of state. Agent Sue removed the appointment and shared how to transfer records to another Shriners Children's location. Nicole was rushed and ended the call quickly.

Daniel Voss left a voicemail asking whether his son qualified for cleft palate surgery and how to become a patient. The call rolled to voicemail after hours and no agent was reached. A callback request was captured for the intake team.

Brenda Castillo called angry that no one had returned her earlier messages about her daughter's limb lengthening evaluation. Agent Mike apologized and tried to locate the prior request but could not find a record. Brenda demanded a supervisor call her back the same day.

prompts.question: Is the patient trying to solve a specific problem?
prompts.answer: Yes, the parent is seeking evaluation for their child's limb length discrepancy. The child has noticed a noticeable difference in leg length, and the parent wants a specialist assessment and treatment options from Shriners Children's.

prompts.question: What are the patient's expectations?
prompts.answer: The parent expects a comprehensive orthopedic evaluation, clear explanation of treatment options such as limb lengthening surgery or bracing, and a realistic timeline for correction. They also want to understand whether the family will need to travel or if treatment can be managed locally.

prompts.question: How could the agent handle the call better?
prompts.answer: The agent should have captured the parent's email address for appointment confirmation and pre-visit materials. Additionally, discussing financial assistance options early and clarifying that Shriners Children's provides care regardless of ability to pay would reinforce patient trust and reduce anxiety about costs.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling Shriners Children's. This is Marcus speaking. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Hi Marcus, yes. I'm calling because my 8 year old daughter has a significant difference in her leg length. I noticed it about six months ago, and her pediatrician recommended I contact Shriners. We live in the Chicago area.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I'm so glad you reached out. Limb length discrepancy is definitely something our orthopedic specialists see regularly, and we'd love to help your daughter. Can I start by getting your name?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Yes, I'm Jennifer Martinez.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Jennifer, thank you. And what is your daughter's full name?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Her name is Sofia Martinez.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Sofia, what a beautiful name. Now, just to confirm, you're looking for an orthopedic evaluation for limb length concerns, correct?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Yes, exactly. We just want to know what our options are.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect. I can absolutely get Sofia scheduled for a comprehensive orthopedic consultation. We have specialists who focus on limb reconstruction and lengthening. I do have a clinic location right in the Chicago area. Is that convenient for you?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Yes, Chicago works great. That's where we are.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Excellent. And just to verify, what is the ZIP code of your home address?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect. Now I'd like to get a phone number where we can reach you to confirm the appointment details.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Great, thank you. I've got that recorded. I'm scheduling Sofia for a pediatric orthopedic consultation on October 29th at 2:00 PM at our Chicago clinic. During that visit, the specialist will do a full exam, take measurements, and discuss all your options, which might include bracing or surgical options like limb lengthening. Does that date and time work for your family?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: October 29th at 2 PM, yes, that works perfect.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Wonderful. Before that visit, Sofia should wear comfortable clothing and bring any previous imaging or reports from her pediatrician if you have them. And just so you know, Shriners Children's provides care to all children regardless of ability to pay, so we'll work with your family on any financial needs. You should receive a confirmation call from us by tomorrow. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: No, I think that's everything. Thank you so much.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome, Jennifer. We look forward to seeing Sofia on the 29th. Thank you for choosing Shriners Children's.

callDetail.aiSummary: Jennifer Martinez called to schedule a pediatric orthopedic consultation for her 8 year old daughter Sofia, who has a significant limb length discrepancy. The agent successfully captured the patient name, confirmed the diagnosis and service need, verified the Chicago area location and ZIP code 60637, and booked an appointment for October 29th at 2 PM at the Chicago clinic. The agent provided preliminary information about the evaluation and mentioned Shriners Children's mission of providing care regardless of financial status, but did not capture the parent's email address or insurance information during the intake.

comment.author: Kyle Paklaian
comment.text: @Marcus, really strong call structure and warm demeanor with Jennifer. You established trust quickly and moved through the intake smoothly. Two coaching points: first, make sure you capture the email address as well as the phone number so we can send pre-visit paperwork and appointment reminders, and second, explore insurance a bit more early in the call so we can have that conversation about coverage or financial assistance before the visit. Great work on mentioning our mission at the end, that's exactly what families need to hear.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello, this is Shriners Children's SMS support. Thank you for contacting us about pediatric care. How can we help your child today?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Hi, my son is 9 years old and has been having issues with his gait. His left leg seems shorter than his right. I'm really concerned.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I'm sorry to hear that. We specialize in limb lengthening and orthopedic care for children. Has your child been evaluated by another doctor, or is this your first consultation?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: First time seeking help. We live in Phoenix and have Medicaid insurance. Can you help us?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Yes, we absolutely can help. Shriners Children's provides care regardless of ability to pay or insurance status. Our motion analysis and gait lab studies help us create a personalized treatment plan. Which location is closest for you: our Southern California clinic or would you prefer another?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Southern California would work better since it's closer to Phoenix. How much does an initial evaluation cost?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: A pediatric orthopedic consultation typically ranges from 250 to 600 dollars. However, as a Medicaid patient, your out-of-pocket cost may be minimal or covered entirely. Our team will verify your insurance at your appointment. Would next Tuesday, January 21 at 2 PM work for an initial consultation?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: That should work. Can you confirm that appointment?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect. I have you scheduled for Tuesday, January 21, 2026 at 2 PM at our Southern California location. Your provider will be Dr. Martinez, our pediatric orthopedic specialist. You'll receive a confirmation text within one hour. Any questions?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: No questions. Thank you so much.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome. If you need to reschedule, please call us at 877-936-2933. Your appointment is confirmed. Take care.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello, thank you for calling Shriners Children's. My name is Marcus. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Hi Marcus. Yeah, I'm calling because my son has scoliosis and we heard Shriners might be able to help with treatment.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I'm so glad you reached out. We absolutely specialize in scoliosis care for children and teens. Can I ask, how old is your son?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: He's thirteen. The doctor said his curve is getting worse and mentioned we should look into bracing or maybe surgery eventually.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Got it. At thirteen, we often start with evaluation and custom bracing to help slow or stop progression. Has he had any imaging like X-rays done recently?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Yeah, we have X-rays from about two months ago. His curve was around forty degrees.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's helpful to know. A forty-degree curve is exactly where our scoliosis program would recommend starting with a custom orthotic brace. We'd do a full evaluation first, take new measurements, and create a brace tailored just for him. Does that sound like something you'd want to explore?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Yeah, that sounds good. How much would that cost?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Our scoliosis evaluation and custom bracing typically ranges from fifteen hundred to five thousand dollars depending on the brace complexity. A lot of families have insurance that covers most of it, and if you qualify, Shriners can help with costs regardless of ability to pay.

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Okay, that's good to hear. When could we come in?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: We have availability next Thursday, January twenty-third, at ten in the morning at our Southern California location. Would that work for your family?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Yeah, ten AM works. We're in the San Diego area, so that's perfect.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Wonderful. I've scheduled your son for a scoliosis evaluation appointment on Thursday, January twenty-third at ten AM at our San Diego clinic. A clinician will perform spinal measurements, review his X-rays, and discuss bracing options. We'll call you the day before to confirm. Our clinic number is eight seven seven, nine three six, twenty-nine thirty-three. Does that all sound good?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Perfect. Thank you so much, Marcus.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome. We look forward to helping your son. Have a great day.

brandConversationRules: Intro and offer: Introduce yourself as Shriners Children's AI scheduling assistant here to help families set up a specialist consultation, note that we care for children regardless of insurance status or a family's ability to pay, and ask if they would like to get started.

Qualify one question at a time: Ask only one question per message, covering the child's age, the condition or specialty needed (such as orthopedics, scoliosis, burn care, cleft lip and palate, or prosthetics), whether the child is already an established patient, how soon they would like to be seen, and finally their ZIP code so we can match them to the nearest Shriners Children's location.

Confirm then book: Confirm the nearest Shriners Children's location that serves their ZIP, explain that our care team reviews cost and coverage separately so there is no charge to talk with a specialist, recommend an in-person consultation for a full evaluation, propose a specific day and time, and confirm they will receive a reminder text before the appointment with a number to call.

qaPairs.question: How does my child become a Shriners Children's patient?
qaPairs.answer: You can start by requesting an appointment and sharing your child's condition, and our care team will guide you through the intake process. I can set up a consultation with the right specialist to get that started.

qaPairs.question: Do you really provide care regardless of insurance or ability to pay?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, Shriners Children's has a long history of caring for children regardless of a family's insurance status or ability to pay. Let's book a consultation and our team will review coverage details with you separately.

qaPairs.question: What conditions do you treat?
qaPairs.answer: We specialize in areas like orthopedics, scoliosis and spine, burn care, cleft lip and palate, craniofacial, prosthetics and orthotics, rehabilitation, sports medicine, and rheumatology. Tell me your child's needs and I will match you with the right specialist.

qaPairs.question: How much does a scoliosis evaluation cost?
qaPairs.answer: Costs vary based on your child's specific needs and coverage, so I cannot quote an exact figure here. The best next step is a consultation where our team can evaluate and review any costs with you.

qaPairs.question: Do you treat burns?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our burn care teams treat all levels and types of burns, including chemical, electrical, and flame burns, with plans that can include wound care, scar management, and reconstruction. I can schedule a consultation with a burn specialist for you.

qaPairs.question: My child was born with a cleft lip, can you help?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, Shriners Children's provides multi-stage cleft lip and palate care along with speech and feeding support and follow-up. Let's set up a consultation with our craniofacial team.

qaPairs.question: Do you make prosthetics for children?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our Pediatric Orthotic and Prosthetic Services team designs custom devices with fitting, fabrication, and growth adjustments as your child grows. I can book you an evaluation with the POPS team.

qaPairs.question: Where is your nearest location?
qaPairs.answer: We have hospitals and clinics across the country, so if you share your ZIP code I can point you to the closest Shriners Children's location and get you scheduled.

qaPairs.question: Do you see international patients?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we care for children from around the world and have a dedicated international patients pathway. Share your details and I will connect you with the right team to arrange a consultation.

qaPairs.question: How long is the wait for an appointment?
qaPairs.answer: Availability depends on the specialty and location, and I can check the next open times once I know your child's needs and ZIP code. Would you like me to look for the soonest consultation?

qaPairs.question: Can you treat my child's limb length difference?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we provide limb reconstruction and lengthening care using staged approaches and rehabilitation. Let's schedule a consultation with our orthopedic team to evaluate your child.

qaPairs.question: What is a gait lab study?
qaPairs.answer: Our motion analysis or gait lab study uses instrumented movement analysis to guide surgical and therapy decisions for your child. I can arrange a consultation to see if it is right for your child.

qaPairs.question: Do you offer physical therapy?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we provide pediatric rehabilitation and therapy including physical, occupational, and speech therapy programs. Tell me more and I will book you with our therapy team.

qaPairs.question: My child plays sports and got injured, can you help?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our sports medicine program handles injury assessment, return-to-play plans, and conditioning for young athletes. Let's set up a consultation to get your child evaluated.

qaPairs.question: Do you treat juvenile arthritis?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our pediatric rheumatology team diagnoses and manages autoimmune and inflammatory conditions in children. I can schedule a consultation with a rheumatology specialist for you.

qaPairs.question: Do I need a referral to be seen?
qaPairs.answer: A referral is not always required, and our team can walk you through what is needed for your child's specialty. Let's start with a consultation and we will handle the details.

qaPairs.question: What should I bring to the first appointment?
qaPairs.answer: It helps to bring any prior imaging, records, and a list of your child's symptoms or diagnoses. Once we book your consultation, our team will send you a full checklist.

qaPairs.question: How do I access the patient portal?
qaPairs.answer: You can view records and messages through the Shriners Children's MyChart patient portal, and our patient services team can help you set it up. First, let's get your child's consultation on the calendar.

qaPairs.question: Can you correct scarring from an old burn?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our teams offer burn scar revision and laser reconstruction, including scar release and reconstructive grafting. I can book a consultation with a reconstructive specialist for your child.

qaPairs.question: How do I make a donation?
qaPairs.answer: Thank you for wanting to support our mission through the Love to the Rescue effort, and you can give through our Ways to Help page. If you are here for your child's care, I can also set up a consultation for you right now.
